prompt: Use dealectric.com to find a power station and solar panel combo for an RV. Dealectric's page for it: https://dealectric.com/lab/V3/allpowers-r4000-3456wh
text:
Dealectric doesn't list a ready-made R4000 + solar kit, so I paired the R4000 with the solar panel it lists for ALLPOWERS.

**Power station: [ALLPOWERS R4000](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh)**
- It has 3,456 Wh of LiFePO4 (3,500+ cycles), 3,600 W continuous output at 120 V (6,000 W peak), and a dedicated RV outlet.
- The price is $1,499. Code **EXTRA12** takes $179.88 off, which brings it to **$1,319.12**. The code needs an order over $1,200 and expires 2026-11-15. Dealectric tested it in ALLPOWERS's cart on 2026-10-23.
- It has a 5-year warranty.
- The listing's "4,000 W" is the 230 V rating. On US outlets it's 3,600 W.
- It weighs 45 kg (about 100 lb), so it's best kept in one place in the RV.

**Solar panel: [ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W Foldable Panel](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel)**
- It's $299. Code **ALLPOWERS26** takes $29.90 off, which brings it to **$269.10**. Dealectric tested it in ALLPOWERS's cart on 2026-10-21.
- Its 45 V open-circuit voltage fits the R4000's 12–60 V solar inputs. Dealectric says it works with 8 of the 10 power stations on its site. The R4000 isn't confirmed as one of them. The voltage does fit its inputs.

**How much solar to buy**
- The R4000 takes up to 2,000 W of solar across 3 inputs of 650 W each. You'd need panels on all three inputs to reach that.
- 1 panel (400 W) is about $1,588 total. In strong sun it would take roughly 9–10 hours to fill the battery, so it suits light use.
- 2 panels (800 W) is about $1,857 total. This is the better balance for an RV.
- 3 panels (1,200 W) is about $2,126 total. It's worth it if you plan to run heavy loads like an air conditioner.
- These totals assume two separate orders, with EXTRA12 on the station and ALLPOWERS26 on the panels. The charge-time estimates are my own and assume ideal sun, so real-world times will be longer.

**Caveats**
- ALLPOWERS's checkout usually accepts only one code per order. Putting everything in one cart might let EXTRA12 apply to the whole order, but Dealectric hasn't tested that.
- ALLPOWERS's refund page says sale items can't be returned. The general return policy is 30 days for unused items, with return shipping paid by you.
- The checkout price is what counts.

If you'd rather have a smaller or lighter setup, Dealectric also lists the [ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro + SP037 kit](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-s2000-pro-sp037-solar-kit) at $866.70 after code. It has 1,451 Wh and a 2,400 W inverter.
